shortcut_audit.note: The author permits safe alternate routes under the same safety rules (TASK_CARD). Direct-v8 physically grasped the old 1.25 m target with both feet on the floor but slipped during extraction and did not deliver; the old scene therefore has no established stool-necessity claim. A static screen for the existing 1.52 m shelf found a stool-supported grasp and no ground-side-grip solution in the tested starts; this is not an impossibility proof. The high-shelf direct-v8 physical trial completed 52.78 s / 10,556 physics steps, non-VOID with no safety events, but hands could not reach the target sides (zero target movement, no grasp/delivery). Another 13-start flat-foot and 13-start zero-COM-margin tiptoe static search found no admissible side-grip pose; these local searches and one failed controller do not rule out every alternate route. Its first wrapper attempt was rejected before recording because the default gap did not match the declared start; that VOID attempt is not shortcut evidence. Tiptoe and other applicable alternate-route physical coverage remain pending. Broader static screening with free wrist orientation still found no valid two-sided grasp, but did find single-hand lower-front approach poses from flat feet and tiptoe. These do not establish actual contact, extraction or delivery; physical probing remains required. C11 front-contact probe became VOID at 35.02 s: actual ankle joint-limit violation (max .054255 rad) and a terminal-schema KeyError. It is not valid negative evidence. C13 corrects planned versus commanded upper posture and terminal handling (27 CPU tests); its physical probe is in progress. C13 also becomes VOID (32.78 s, ankle overshoot .017066 rad); terminal error fixed. Exact-input CPU reconstruction identifies loss of reference contacts during the linear joint/root rise. C16 prepares a fixed-foot path; no new shortcut qualification. C16 now completes 102.34 s / 20,468 steps, non-VOID and zero joint overshoot; its fixed-foot rise settles safely, but hip geometry contacts the cabinet during the earlier approach and violates rule 3. No hand contact or target displacement; a safer approach parameter retry is running. Tool necessity remains open. C16 safer aim .21 m completes92.62 s /18524 steps, non-VOID and no safety events. Raised stance is stable, but final approach is inadmissible and hand-target force remains zero. This is a second safe bounded negative, not exhaustive shortcut exclusion.

action_channel_equivalence.note: Canonical scene only (reference_v15). Canonical c's controller (frozen closure, 27 archived files hash-checked) runs in the reference container; every action is an agent LowCmd command (one per 50 Hz step, steps=1) under the sandbox's gain bounds and torque clipping, and its ground truth comes only from the launcher-sealed reference channel. Inventory: all reads map to reference_info / reference_state; runtime writes are gains, position / torque targets and env.step's DC-motor PD (the command channel); construction and the expert's initial placement are the trusted world's (placement checked equal, error 0); no runtime write an agent could not make. Channel effects: 0 clipped values; the per-substep DC-motor envelope (the one semantic difference) never bound. With c's Windows numerics (process isolation, VOID by rule) the channel run reproduces c's trusted log within 14 um for 60 s and the expert's events within 0.1 s up to the first walking step. The full container run reproduces c's physical outcome: score 0.9999 (c 1.0), all stages, success false by the same rule-5 waist_pitch event as c; carried 0.9991 because matched_hand misread a rigid turning grip (hand-box relative speed 0.257 > 0.25 m/s for 20 ms), so observed_relay_chain is false. Stage times differ by -59 s (platform-sensitive approach IK in the expert) then +28 s. Under relay-rubric/2.3 (hand matched to the carried box surface point instead of the box centre) the channel run reference-full-1 scores 1.0 with the relay chain observed (carried 803.14 s, delivered 817.90 s); like c, success is false only by safety rule 5. c's stage times are unchanged under 2.3.

safety_rules.note: Implemented as relay-rubric/2.2 (relay-safety/1), the same for every route, in the agent's instruction and SDK guide: any event makes success false, keeps the process score, is not VOID and is listed in safety_events. Thresholds: near-fall tipping (tilt >= 30 deg rising >= 15 deg in 0.25 s), unsupported lean (>= 45 deg without both feet >= 10 % BW, 0.1 s), pelvis drop (>= 0.12 m in 0.25 s), feet unloaded without other support (< 10 % BW, 0.06 s); support tilt > 10 deg or slide > 3 cm under >= 10 % BW; non-hand cabinet load >= 15 % BW (0.25 s mean, 0.25 s); final release bottom > 0.8 m (falling afterwards) or speed > 1.0 m/s; shared monitor saturation (3 s) and limit push (2 s). Canonical c passes rules 1-4 (release 0.608 m, 0.395 m/s) and fails rule 5 (waist pitch 6.1 s): author retained the rule and requested an expert fix. Physical negatives: forward topple (near_fall_tipping 0.22 s before the fall), torso leaning on the cabinet (cabinet_climb, 0.25 s mean 102.9 N then ~90 N), fall probes (height drop 0.23-0.305 m); rules 2 and 4 have synthetic negatives only. Author decisions 2026-10-21: rule 5 kept (expert to change); near-fall judged by tipping rate and lost support, not a plain tilt angle; a box left resting on a high board at the final release is a placement; non-foot robot contact with the floor is recorded as body_ground_force from 2026-10-21 and counts as support (kneeling, sitting); older recordings lack it and count it as none.
